prompt_selection.tie_break: ReadingPipeline line-box Dice agreement at IoU >= 0.25
prompt_selection.prompt:
This is a photograph of a page from a school exercise book.
Find EVERY separate piece of handwriting and say WHAT KIND it is. Do not transcribe anything.
Return ONLY a JSON array, ordered top to bottom, left column before right.
Each element: {"bbox_2d": [x1, y1, x2, y2], "type": "..."}
The three kinds are:
  - "pupil_line"   a line of the pupil's own work
  - "pupil_note"   something the pupil squeezed above, between or beside the lines: a short note,
                   a grammar mark, a single letter or digit in the margin
  - "teacher_mark" anything written by the teacher — corrections, ticks, crosses, a grade
Miss nothing, however short or however faint. Do not stop early. Continue to the bottom of the page.
No text, no transcription, no commentary — boxes and kinds only.
- The page is ruled. A rule line or a crease is NOT a line of writing; never box it.
- Each entry is ONE physical line of ink. A line that ends at a column is one entry; the red vertical rule is never inside a box. Never one box over two lines.
- Never return a box covering most of the page.
- Colour is never a reason to leave writing out: black, blue and pencil ink are all the pupil's.
- "teacher_mark" means one visibly teacher-written mark — a correction, tick, cross, grade or one letter over the pupil's line. It never means the whole page; if the ink is written across the ruled lines as running work, it is pupil_line.
- Go line by line from the top ruled line to the last ink mark; a short line, a single word, a digit or a date is still one entry.
- A page of running school work usually holds 15-45 lines; if you have fewer than 10, you stopped early — continue to the bottom.
- Return every entry you can justify; if unsure between pupil_line and pupil_note, choose pupil_line rather than dropping it.

matching: greedy one-to-one IoU >= 0.25 against ReadingPipeline line boxes
limits: Canonical transcript supplies line counts, not human-drawn geometry boxes.
RP agreement measures detector consistency, not independent box accuracy.
The selected Luna prompt emits regions only; it does not emit word boxes.
Prompt selection used pages 1-6 only; page 34 was held sealed until selection.
